label: Formal object of a favouring: the ranking that measures its kind of operation
term: formal object of a favouring (obj φ)
definition: A formal-object assignment obj gives, for each favouring profile φ, a ranking of candidates in each variation scenario: the standard by which φ's kind of operation is measured (lane P's per-bearer reading of the standard of favouring). For a will (rational appetite) it is the good, read as the value order; for a natural tendency it is the end of the nature, which may be an end content D or, on the imitability-exemplar account, the good. It is the formal object of the kind, not the favouring's particular content: with obj φ := φ every favouring would trivially make exactly its object's verdicts, and that reading is not intended. Example: a one-domain knower is measured by truth, the object of knowing as such, not by the truths of its domain. In Lean the assignment is a parameter; nothing in the type stops a degenerate assignment, so this record states the intended constraint.
note: Stipulative analyst notion (#2145 lane H3), attribution deferred. It is a parameter of PureFavouringTracksItsObject and ActualRootFavouringObjectIsValue and has no Lean declaration of its own. The per-bearer reading was introduced and tested in lane P (docs/notes/causal-perfection-transfer.md, section 'When is a restriction of content a limitation?', A4). See docs/notes/causal-perfection-transfer.md, section 'Natural or rational appetite? The purity premises and the object of an original source's favouring'.
